Download a BFS file

Source: R/bfs_download_asset.R
bfs_download_asset.Rd

Download any file of the BFS (Excel, CSV, PX, PDF, zip, ...) from the DAM API (https://dam-api.bfs.admin.ch/hub/swagger-ui/index.html) with its asset number or its BFS number. Use it for the tables of bfs_get_catalog_tables(), or for datasets too large for bfs_get_data().

Usage

bfs_download_asset(
  number_asset = NULL,
  number_bfs = NULL,
  destfile,
  quiet = TRUE,
  mode = "wb",
  handle = curl::new_handle()
)

Arguments

number_asset

The asset number of the file, e.g. "24025646". It is the number_asset column of bfs_get_catalog_tables() and bfs_get_catalog_data(), and the number at the end of the "assetdetail" URLs of the BFS website.

number_bfs

The BFS number of the file, e.g. "px-x-1502040100_131". Use either number_asset or number_bfs.

destfile

Path of the downloaded file.

quiet

If FALSE, show the download progress.

mode, handle

Passed to curl::curl_download().

Value

The path of the downloaded file. Returns NULL if there is no internet connection.

See also

bfs_get_asset_metadata(), bfs_get_catalog_tables()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # interactive()
# a PX file, read it with pxR::read.px()
bfs_download_asset(
  number_bfs = "px-x-1502040100_131",
  destfile = file.path(tempdir(), "px-x-1502040100_131.px")
)
}
